question: What is a primary benefit of automated patient beds regarding nursing personnel?

options.A: They completely replace the need for bedside nursing assessments.
options.B: They lower the incidence of work-related musculoskeletal injuries by reducing manual strain.
options.C: They eliminate all documentation requirements for patient repositioning.
options.D: They allow nurses to work entirely remotely from home.

explanation: Automated beds help mitigate physical strain on nurses who traditionally perform manual repositioning and transfers, thereby lowering musculoskeletal injuries. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h1)

question: How do smart beds differ fundamentally from traditional hospital beds?

options.A: They rely exclusively on manual hand cranks for all adjustments.
options.B: They utilize motorized mechanisms and digital interfaces for automated positioning and monitoring.
options.C: They are constructed entirely from lightweight plastic materials.
options.D: They are only permitted for use in outpatient pediatric clinics.

explanation: Smart beds utilize motorized mechanisms and digital interfaces to allow automated positioning, height adjustment, and continuous health monitoring, unlike traditional beds. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the clinical purpose of integrated load cells in smart beds?

options.B: To track patient weight accurately without moving them to a separate scale
options.C: To automatically lock the bed wheels during an emergency
options.D: To administer intravenous fluids at a calculated rate

explanation: Integrated load cells and weighing systems enable accurate weight tracking without requiring the patient to move, which is vital for monitoring fluid balance. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which component is responsible for powering the articulation and height adjustments of a smart bed?
explanation: Electric actuators are the core components that power articulation, allowing smooth adjustments of the bed sections without manual exertion. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which type of smart bed is specifically designed for high-fall-risk patients to minimize injury from rolls?
explanation: Low beds are designed specifically for high-fall-risk patients because they can descend very close to the floor, minimizing injury if a patient rolls out. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h3)

question: What features are typically found in critical care smart beds?

options.A: Ligature-resistant casings and tamper-proof locks only
options.B: Rotation therapy, percussion, vibration, and advanced scale systems
options.C: Manual hand cranks and wooden side rails
options.D: Fixed height settings with no articulation options

explanation: Critical care smart beds are equipped with complex rotation therapy, continuous lateral rotation, percussion, vibration, and advanced integrated scale systems. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why are critical care beds with continuous lateral rotation therapy beneficial for mechanically ventilated patients?

options.A: They eliminate the need for oral hygiene care.
options.B: They assist in preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia by promoting pulmonary drainage.
options.D: They replace the need for mechanical ventilators.

explanation: Continuous lateral rotation therapy assists in preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia by promoting pulmonary drainage in immobile, ventilated patients. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which patient group requires a bariatric smart bed configuration?

options.A: Patients requiring continuous lateral rotation for pulmonary hygiene
options.B: Patients with high weight capacities needing reinforced frames and powered transfer assistance
options.C: Patients recovering from mild outpatient dental surgery
options.D: Pediatric patients admitted for routine observation

explanation: Bariatric patients require specialized automated beds with reinforced frames, wider surfaces, and high weight capacities to ensure safety and support. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h4)

question: How do smart beds assist in the prevention of pressure injuries?

options.A: By automatically applying chemical barrier creams to the skin
options.B: Through continuous pressure redistribution, automated micro-repositioning, and pressure sensors
options.C: By cooling the room temperature to prevent sweating
options.D: By completely eliminating the need for manual skin assessments

explanation: Smart beds mitigate pressure injuries through continuous pressure redistribution, automated micro-repositioning, and sensors that alert staff to prolonged immobility. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the function of multi-zone exit detection systems in smart bed safety?

options.A: To alert nursing staff at different stages of egress, such as sitting up or standing, before a fall happens
options.B: To automatically lock the room doors when a patient tries to leave
options.C: To extinguish fires in the event of an electrical short circuit
options.D: To track the exact GPS location of the patient within the hospital

explanation: Multi-zone exit detection sensors can be programmed to alert staff at various stages of egress, allowing proactive intervention before a fall occurs. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h5)

question: When should a nurse perform mechanical and safety assessments of an automated patient bed?

options.A: Only upon initial discharge from the hospital
options.B: Upon admission and during every shift change
options.C: Once a month by the biomedical engineering department
options.D: Only after a patient experiences a fall

explanation: Nurses must evaluate the bed's mechanical integrity, electrical cords, and safety features upon admission and during every shift change. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a potential safety hazard associated with improper side rail use on smart beds?

options.B: They can transform into restraints or entrapment hazards if used incorrectly.
options.C: They interfere with the bed's weighing scale accuracy.
options.D: They automatically disable the nurse call system.

explanation: Improper side rail use can create patient entrapment hazards or act as unauthorized physical restraints, requiring careful nursing assessment. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is a primary advantage of integrating smart beds with electronic health record (EHR) systems?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for bedside physical examinations.
options.B: It streams bed-generated data directly to medical records, streamlining documentation and reducing errors.
options.C: It allows the bed to automatically administer prescribed medications.
options.D: It prevents the bed from ever experiencing mechanical malfunctions.

explanation: Direct data transmission to EHR systems streamlines clinical documentation, minimizes manual charting errors, and saves nursing time. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h7)

question: How do central nursing station dashboards assist staff regarding smart bed management?

options.A: They provide a real-time overview of ward safety, highlighting disarmed alarms or unlatched brakes.
options.B: They automatically order dietary trays for patients.
options.C: They control the temperature of the hospital laundry room.
options.D: They perform routine equipment maintenance without human intervention.

explanation: Dashboards provide a macro-level view of ward safety, highlighting items like disarmed alarms or unlatched brakes across multiple rooms. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the appropriate initial nursing action when a smart bed experiences an electronic articulation failure?

options.A: Immediately discard the bed as hazardous waste.
options.B: Perform basic troubleshooting by checking power sources, circuit breakers, and cable connections.
options.C: Manually dismantle the internal electrical actuators.
options.D: Transfer the patient to the floor until repairs are completed.

explanation: Nurses should first perform basic troubleshooting like checking power sources and cable connections before escalating to biomedical engineering. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h8)

question: Why is careful attention required when cleaning and disinfecting automated patient beds?

options.A: Harsh chemicals will dissolve the metal frame instantly.
options.B: Complex beds have crevices and electrical touchpoints that must be disinfected without allowing fluid ingress.
options.C: Cleaning must only be performed while the patient is sleeping in the bed.
options.D: Disinfectants erase the memory of the mattress pressure sensors.

explanation: Staff must clean complex joints and touchpoints thoroughly while preventing fluid ingress into electrical housings to avoid short circuits. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T7#GNS212_U4_T7_h8)
